1: A two-port: anything with an input and an output
2: Send a wave a1 into port 1
3: Part of it comes back out of port 1 (b1), part comes out of port 2 (b2)
4: S-parameters are ratios: what comes out divided by what went in
5: The name says where: S out, in.  S21 = out at port 2, in at port 1
6: Now the other way: source on port 2, port 1 terminated with 50 Ω
7: Four numbers describe the two-port: reflections on the diagonal, transmissions across
8: Ratios are given in dB: 10 · log₁₀ of the power ratio
9: dB makes tiny and huge ratios readable on one axis, and ratios become subtractions
11: Passive parts work both ways (S21 = S12), an amplifier only one way
12: Over frequency, e.g. a 1 GHz low-pass filter
13: Below 1 GHz the signal passes (S21 ≈ 0 dB), above it is blocked
14: What does not pass comes back: S11 rises where S21 falls
15: The SNA measures powers in dBm, so S11 in dB is just a subtraction
16: Directional coupler and log detector measure these powers, calibration removes the SNA's own losses
